name: COMO Alpina Dolomites
positioning: Modern ski-in ski-out mountain hotel with a COMO Shambhala spa on South Tyrol's Alpe di Siusi plateau, set at 1,800 metres in the UNESCO-listed Dolomites
best_for: Skiers who want direct ski-in ski-out access in the Dolomiti Superski region
Wellness travellers who want daily yoga and a full sauna and pool area
Hikers and cyclists wanting guided mountain experiences in summer

facts.text: The hotel sits on South Tyrol's Alpe di Siusi, a high-altitude plateau in the Dolomites.
The hotel is cradled by the sheer cliffs of a UNESCO Natural World Heritage site in northern Italy.
The hotel is set at an altitude of 1,800 metres.
The property is near the mountain station of the Siusi-Alpe di Siusi cableway.
Guests enter through an entryway designed to resemble a rock crevice.
Rooms combine soft colours with quality furnishings finessed by South Tyrol's traditional artisans.
The Dolomites Chalet Suite is a two-bedroom suite with a curved layout.
Access to the COMO Shambhala wellness facilities, including indoor and outdoor thermal pools, is complimentary during a stay.
The spa has a Finnish and bio-herb sauna with two Kneipp basins.
The spa has a relaxation room with single and double waterbeds.
The hotel offers daily yoga, Pilates and guided meditation sessions suitable for all levels.
The resort has three restaurants and a bar.

highlights.text: The hotel offers direct ski-in ski-out access, within the Dolomiti Superski region of Val Gardena.
The exterior is clad with quartzite and wood, a nod to the mineral-rich terrain.
The spa offers a South Tyrol-inspired hay bath.
A guided Sellaronda ski tour across four mountain passes is offered as a group tour in the complimentary weekly programme.
The Mountain Suite has a clean-burning bio-ethanol fireplace and a private infrared sauna.

considerations.text: The hotel operates seasonally, in winter from December to March and in summer and autumn from June to October.
Access by private car on Alpe di Siusi is not allowed from 9am to 5pm without a transit permit.
WhataHotel notes that the remote mountain location requires transportation planning.
